issue_context.title: NullableConverter does not flow serialization state
issue_context.body: The System.Text.Json `NullableConverter<T>` incorrectly declares itself as a value converter, even though this only applies to cases where the `T` type uses a value converter itself. This means that nullable struct serialization does not flow serialization state correctly, which can result in async serialization not performing as expected.

review_comments: This renames a property I should have renamed in #65224 and matches the naming convention by the equivalent property in `ReadStackFrame`.

could you just pass in `value` directly here rather than `out T element`? wouldn't it return null when the read returns false? this could then be simplified to:

```suggestion
            return _elementConverter.TryRead(ref reader, typeof(T), options, ref state, out value);
```
`value` is of type `Nullable<T>` whereas the element converter is of type `T` so that wouldn't work unfortunately.
Should there be a non-IAsyncEnumerable test added that can verify a larger, nullable POCO (as a value type)?
Nullable POCOs still work, however they don't flow the state. This becomes more evident in the case of IAE which simply fails serialization.
I assume the ConverterStrategy is determined by the value held by Nullable? I.e. it can be Value, Object, Collection.
Strengthens an assertion that should have been changed via #65224.
Using an auto property is intentional here. The particular property is invoked by the base constructor before `_elementConverter` can be populated.
